His own K-DOCS page (https://www.drjamescaufman.com/k-docs, served from https://violet-scarlet-dasj.squarespace.com/k-docs, fetched 2026-09-10, sha256 86f71456fd586175a22f8694e0e90828c5e28f35b1ee172b9f4c41eaca38aed3) publishes the complete 50-item scale, its instructions and its five anchors in full, with no copyright notice, no fee, no non-commercial clause, no no-derivatives clause and no bar on reproduction or redistribution anywhere on the page. The ONLY permission-adjacent sentence is a grant, not a restriction: "Many people reach out to me to ask permission to use the scale. I am happy to give permission. Just drop me a line.", immediately followed by "I have linked the relevant articles and the scale here so all of the information is in one place." Read strictly, "ask permission" sits in the same family as the permission-required trigger in SKILL.md's block list, and that is why this is flagged rather than treated as settled. Read as written it reserves nothing -- it names no use he would refuse, imposes no condition, and he is himself the party distributing the wording publicly and unconditionally. SKILL.md requires a quotable RESTRICTION for a block and says silence is permission and not to block on suspicion; there is no restriction here to quote. Shipped on that basis. A round may never write a register 'ship' or 'ship_with_note' row, so none was written -- this is escalated to the human for a register verdict. Note also that what IRW ships in the base fields is Miroshnik et al.'s administered Russian from their CC BY 4.0 OSF deposit, but the *_translated columns carry Kaufman's own published English verbatim, so a block would reach both. The article carrying the original publication is APA-copyright, but per SKILL.md a copyright notice on a journal article is a notice about that article, not a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case).

(1) The administered questionnaire offered THREE responses per item (TAK / NIE / NIE WIEM = yes / no / don't know); the IRW processing script (data/rzeszutek_2020_wwii_grandparent_trauma.py) drops "don't know" as missing, so the live table stores only 0=NIE and 1=TAK and only those two option rows are shipped. (2) The instrument asks each of the 29 event questions in a shared grandmother/grandfather stem, laid out as one row per event with separate YES/NO/DON'T KNOW columns for (PRA)BABCIA and (PRA)DZIADEK, under a mother's-side and a father's-side table.
